unchanged_original_task.problem: Use dd^c=(i/(2 pi))partial barpartial; X is connected and compact. All potentials are genuine canonical psh-plus-smooth representatives. Assume n>=2. Let h be a smooth Hermitian metric and dV a smooth positive probability volume. Let G_h consist of all positive (n-1,n-1)-currents T with dd^c T=0 and integral h wedge T=1. Write sigma_T=h wedge T; in an h-unitary frame let P_T be the positive Hermitian matrix density characterized by beta wedge T=(1/n)tr(B P_T)d sigma_T, tr(P_T)=n, for B the h-relative matrix of any smooth (1,1)-form beta. The determinant measure Gamma_0(T)=(dV/h^n)^(1/n)det(P_T)^(1/n)sigma_T is absolutely continuous with respect to dV. Define k_T=d Gamma_0(T)/dV. For smooth strictly positive T=gamma^(n-1), k_T=(gamma^n/dV)^((n-1)/n). The family G_h includes singular and degenerate currents, and the endpoint is over all currents, not only smooth exact maximizers. Define v_minus(h) as the infimum of the total bounded-potential Monge-Ampere masses over all bounded genuine h-psh potentials. Original problem: find geometric conditions beyond the known metric identities implying the uniform endpoint sup_{T in G_h}||k_T||_{L^(n/(n-1))(dV)}<infinity and identify how they exclude primitive elliptic lower-mass degeneration. The exact known equivalence is v_minus(h)>0 iff this endpoint is finite, with the supremum equal to v_minus(h)^(-1/n). Every strictly smaller exponent has a universal uniform estimate. The known metric-identity criterion is geometric: if X admits a Hermitian g with dd^c g=dd^c(g^2)=0, then every Hermitian h>=c g has v_minus(h)>=c^n integral g^n and endpoint constant at most c^(-1)(integral g^n)^(-1/n). In particular every Hermitian background on a compact Kahler manifold or compact complex surface has the endpoint, even if h itself lacks the identities. The standard scalar Hopf threefold also has the already known positive lower mass six and infinite upper mass; merely repeating its known endpoint is insufficient. A balanced threefold with finite upper bounded-potential mass may have zero lower mass and fail the endpoint even on smooth positive tests. Balancedness plus bounded upper mass is therefore insufficient. A bound for one smooth exact maximizer or even a chosen family of maximizers does not bound all tests or all near-maximizing sequences. No candidate geometric hypothesis, estimate or proof is supplied.
unchanged_original_task.completionCriteria: Prove new nonvacuous geometric sufficient conditions beyond the listed metric identities for the full normalized-current endpoint, checking their exclusion of the known lower-mass degeneration. Equivalently prove a quantitative positive lower mass for every bounded admissible potential under the new conditions. A restricted-test estimate, restatement of the equivalence, or a repeated known case is insufficient. Fully specify all geometric hypotheses and actual examples; retain any unresolved broader scope. Check indispensable external premises at primary sources and independently reconstruct the complete proof.

mathematical_application_assessment: For a principal elliptic bundle over a Kahler surface with type(1,1) curvature pair alpha,beta and Q=alpha^2+beta^2 nonzero and nonnegative, construct g=pi*omega+s i eta wedge bareta. Direct calculation gives ddc g=-s pi*Q/(2pi), ddc(g^2)=0 and exact mass V=3s A_E integral omega^2. Canonical bounded BT energy proves every bounded-potential mass equals V+(3s/(2pi)) integral E_u pi*Q>=V. Intrinsic Radon matrix comparison then uses the task-given endpoint duality for all singular and degenerate currents. Direct quotient/period calculations and no-LCK obstruction establish the examples independently.

clause_assessment.requested: Geometric hypotheses beyond the known first-two-powers-closed metric identities
clause_assessment.proved: The elliptic bundle curvature-pair sign Q>=0,Q not identically0 constructs a metric with nonzero ddc g and excludes every pluriclosed metric. Explicit non-Hopf negative-line-bundle quotients and Calabi-Eckmann tau=A+iB with A<0,B>0 satisfy the condition; the latter have no LCK or Vaisman metric.

clause_assessment.requested: Uniform endpoint over the entire original normalized-current family
clause_assessment.proved: For every Hermitian h>=c g, v_minus(h)>=c^3 V and every singular or degenerate T in G_h satisfies norm(k_T,3/2)<=c^-1 V^-1/3. No exact-maximizer restriction or averaging of tests is used.

clause_assessment.requested: Quantitative positivity for every bounded admissible potential
clause_assessment.proved: The exact signed cubic identity gives v_minus(g)=V>0 for all bounded genuine canonical g-psh potentials, with no common oscillation bound or BMP premise.

clause_assessment.requested: Explain exclusion of the primitive elliptic lower-mass degeneration
clause_assessment.proved: A nonzero primitive real(1,1) curvature on a surface has negative square. Thus the primitive curvature pair has Q of the opposite sign and violates the geometric antecedent. No universal primitive-bundle lower-mass value is inferred.
